items.text: We first need to understand the short but hidden history behind the plastics industry and how it became deeply rooted in our daily lives. <break time="0.8s" /> Before plastic, people lived more sustainably, with far fewer waste problems than we face today. <break time="0.8s" /> However, after the invention of plastic, its rapid adoption during World War II, and its explosion into consumer goods, plastic was everywhere. <break time="0.8s" /> The growing industry came to symbolize the convenience and prosperity of the American dream. <break time="0.8s" /> This dream came with a price. <break time="0.8s" /> Over time, people began to notice the environmental impact, and the early seeds of todays environmental movement were planted. <break time="0.8s" /> However, the plastics industry was quick to counter these concerns, launching campaigns that presented recycling as the solution to all our problems. <break time="0.8s" /> They pushed the idea that pollution was the fault of consumers, not the corporations flooding the market with plastic.
